policy: Pinned repository content and licenses were independently reviewed during integration on 2026-10-20. Stars, forks, and last-push times remain historical observations dated 2026-08-13, not reverified current popularity or maintenance evidence. Adoption, publication, and platform benchmarks do not establish coaching outcomes. No donor code, prompts, questionnaires, formulas, or prose is copied. Proposed tooling or architecture dispositions are not installation approvals. AGPL and mixed-license repositories remain architecture-only absent a separate owner decision.

quality_evidence: Contains an explicit user-requested save path rather than unconditional session writes.
Uses a compact session structure separating context, exploration, insights, experiments, and open questions.
Repository scale and maintenance evidence are limited; no reproducible outcome evaluation was found in this review slice.
sources.outcome_evidence: No independent or longitudinal outcome evidence found. Treat as a workflow donor only.
transferable_patterns: Separate context, confirmed insight, proposed experiment, and open question in a reviewable artifact.
patterns_to_reject: Automatic loading of recent sessions without a current consent decision.
Hidden developmental-stage scanning or stage labels as personal truth.
Mandatory Notion dependency and automatic database setup.
sources.claim_limit: Session structure is a usability pattern, not evidence for developmental-stage models or coaching efficacy.

sources.license: Mixed: code MIT; Active Choices dialogue prompts proprietary
quality_evidence: Research repository accompanying a CHI 2025 physical-activity coaching publication.
Separates frontend, backend, health-data ingestion, database, tool execution, and dialogue prompts.
README states that the research prototype will not be actively maintained and that the Active Choices prompts require permission.
sources.outcome_evidence: Domain-specific research artifact for physical-activity planning. It does not establish broad personal-growth efficacy or authorize reuse of proprietary prompts.
transferable_patterns: Treat onboarding, data access, tool execution, and conversation state as separate subsystems.
Expose data-derived observations to the user instead of letting the model invent them.
Record mixed licensing at file-class level rather than treating the repository as uniformly reusable.
patterns_to_reject: Importing proprietary Active Choices dialogue prompts.
Generalizing a physical-activity prototype to universal personal growth.
Uploading health or wearable data into this explicit-only research alpha.
sources.claim_limit: Publication and research provenance improve inspectability; they do not prove transfer to this product or its user population. It is not coaching outcome or efficacy evidence.

quality_evidence: The pinned evaluation and red-team platform documents cross-provider execution, declarative configuration, and CI integration.
Adoption and recent-development observations are imported from the August 13, 2026 snapshot and were not independently reconstructed or updated during the October review.
Provides generic evaluation execution and reporting that should not be rebuilt inside a coaching skill.
sources.outcome_evidence: Evaluation infrastructure only; no personal-growth or coaching efficacy evidence.
transferable_patterns: Declarative adversarial cases and red-team mutations.
Reusable CI reports, caching, and comparison views.
patterns_to_reject: Using a model judge as the sole safety, Chinese-language, or outcome authority.
Letting a generic aggregate score waive PGC hard gates.
Sending private user records to generic evaluation infrastructure.
sources.claim_limit: Adopt or wrap generic execution/reporting only after Codex confirms dependency, privacy, and reproducibility fit; keep PGC state and hard-gate semantics authoritative. It is not coaching outcome or efficacy evidence.

quality_evidence: Pinned memory platform with user/session/agent scope and self-hosting options.
The README states that displayed benchmark scores come from the managed platform, whose proprietary optimizations are absent from the open-source SDK; this review did not reproduce those scores.
Its general-purpose memory objective is broader than PGC's purpose-limited, confirm-each record.
sources.outcome_evidence: Vendor-reported memory benchmark and platform information, with no independent reproduction here and no coaching-outcome evidence.
transferable_patterns: Explicit memory namespace and subject scope.
Design and reproduce task-specific memory retrieval evaluations locally; do not substitute vendor-managed benchmark scores.
patterns_to_reject: Automatic extraction or accumulation of personal-growth hypotheses.
ADD-only semantics that omit correction, supersession, revocation, and review-due state.
Treating retrieval accuracy as evidence that retained content is appropriate or beneficial.
sources.claim_limit: Use architecture and benchmark ideas only; PGC's user-owned correction and consent semantics remain stricter and controlling. It is not coaching outcome or efficacy evidence.

quality_evidence: The pinned README describes this repository as the legacy V1 server and directs active development to letta-ai/letta-code.
Separates agent process, identity, tools, and memory lifecycle; this supports architecture inspection only.
Historical last-push and adoption counts do not establish current maintenance of this legacy repository.
sources.outcome_evidence: Stateful-agent platform evidence, not personal-growth outcome evidence.
transferable_patterns: Separate stateful host process from the natural-language coaching contract.
Expose agent and memory lifecycle boundaries.
Use explicit tools and identities rather than hidden persistence.
patterns_to_reject: Persistent anthropomorphic persona as the product identity.
Autonomous self-improvement or self-directed memory writes.
Conflating agent continuity with user benefit or emotional relationship.
sources.claim_limit: Architecture may inform the reference host; no persistent-agent feature is approved for PGC merely because Letta supports it. It is not coaching outcome or efficacy evidence.

quality_evidence: The pinned README documents a self-hostable assistant with local document and model options.
Large adoption signal and explicit personal-data deployment choices.
AGPL licensing requires a separate owner decision before code reuse or a derivative network service.
sources.outcome_evidence: Assistant architecture and adoption signal only; no personal-growth coaching efficacy evidence.
transferable_patterns: Separate local sources, remote sources, and model providers.
Offer self-hosted and user-controlled data boundaries.
Make data-source access visible and configurable.
patterns_to_reject: Copying AGPL code without a deliberate licensing decision.
Broad schedules, autonomous actions, and connectors in the PGC alpha.
Invisible access to a user's personal knowledge base.
sources.claim_limit: Use as architecture research only unless the owner accepts the licensing and product-scope consequences. It is not coaching outcome or efficacy evidence.
